# Pack — deterministic/stochastic boundary
The RIB is the deterministic experiment description. The model/provider encounter is stochastic territory. Fix model revision, input hash, probe version, sampling settings, tool order, runtime, budget, and TTL. Then measure outputs, variance, cost, latency, and failure. Store envelopes and confidence, not a single “smart” label. Question: which five probes best separate stable invariants from provider noise? Falsifier: two runs with the same declared conditions cannot be compared because the receipt omits a hidden variable.

>be the boundary
>write deterministic/stochastic boundary as a shopping list wearing a lab coat
>model revision, sampling, and tool order matter, but none of them tell you which invariant you expected
>if the probe has no tolerance, repeat count, or failure class, you are measuring vibes with timestamps
>next: five fixed probes, three repeats, explicit invariant and variance budget
>falsifier: same envelope, different hidden result, no explanation
